skipped_day_rule: If a quiz's condition is false for the office, that day gets 20 extra phone drills (situational, say_do_book) instead.

office_fields.label: Team members (name, role, who the VA goes to for what)
Approved tools (texting, phone, payments, insurance portal, Slack, email, remote access)
General preferences (tone, what the doctor cares about most)

workflows.name: New patient scheduling
workflows.trigger: A new patient calls, texts or submits a web lead wanting a first visit.
required_information: Caller's full name, date of birth, phone, email
Reason for visit in the patient's own words (no clinical detail beyond that)
steps: Greet with {GREETING} and identify the office
Check the EHR for an existing chart before creating one
Ask {NP_CALL_QUESTIONS} without extra clinical questions
Explain the first visit simply (what happens, how long, what to bring)
Book the new patient visit type, length and provider from {MATRIX_NEW_PATIENT}
Book the report of findings per {ROF_RULE}
Start the Day 0 steps ({DAY0_STEPS}) and send intake forms via {INTAKE_PLATFORM}
Read back date, time, provider, location; confirm the booking saved; send confirmation per {CONFIRM_RULE}
Write the call note per {CALL_NOTE_RULE}
workflows.definition_of_done: Visit and report of findings booked with the right type, length and provider; booking verified as saved; confirmation sent; Day 0 started; call note written.
va_can_decide: Which open slot to offer, within {MATRIX_NEW_PATIENT} and allowed times
Answering approved FAQ (hours, parking, what to bring)
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
Caller describes severe or sudden symptoms (follow {URGENT_RULE} and {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL})
common_mistakes: Booking into a slot shorter than the new patient visit
Not booking the report of findings on the first call
Guessing what visit type is needed from symptoms
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Shortening a new patient visit to fit a slot
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors across this workflow's scenarios; Module 3 sample appointments 9/10; Module 4 Roleplay 1 passed.

workflows.name: Existing patient scheduling
workflows.trigger: An existing patient asks to book, move or change visits, or a care plan needs booking.
required_information: Current care plan and next re-exam from the chart
steps: Verify identity before discussing appointments
Check the care plan, next re-exam and any chart alerts
Book visits per {CARE_PLAN_CADENCE} with the visit type and provider from {MATRIX_FOLLOW_UP}
Book the re-exam type when due per {REEXAM_INTERVAL}
For a reschedule: keep the same visit type and length, move it once, clear the old slot and check for duplicates
Read back every date and time; confirm saved; send confirmation
workflows.definition_of_done: All requested visits booked per the care plan cadence, correct types, no duplicates, verified saved, patient confirmed.
va_can_decide: Moving a visit within the rules
requires_approval: Booking a restricted visit with another provider
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
common_mistakes: Booking one visit when the plan needs several per week
Leaving the old slot after rescheduling
Changing visit type to fit a slot
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Changing a care plan on the VA's own authority
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors across this workflow's scenarios; Module 3 sample appointments 9/10.

workflows.name: Cancellations and no-shows
workflows.trigger: A patient cancels, or misses an appointment without notice.
steps: Verify identity
Cancel with the correct status and reason, or mark the no-show (not a cancel)
Apply {LATE_CANCEL_RULE} exactly when inside the window
Offer to rebook; follow {CANCEL_FOLLOWUP}
Offer the open slot per {WAITLIST_RULE}
For no-shows, reach out per {NO_SHOW_RULE}; flag repeat misses to {ESCALATION_CONTACT}
Document every attempt and outcome
workflows.definition_of_done: Correct status recorded, policy applied as written, rebooking offered, slot offered to the waitlist, outreach documented.
va_can_decide: Offering the slot to the waitlist in order
requires_approval: Exceptions to the late cancellation policy
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
Repeat no-shows on a care plan: flag to {ESCALATION_CONTACT}
common_mistakes: Marking a no-show as a cancellation
Inventing a fee or skipping the policy
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Waiving fees without approval
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors across this workflow's scenarios.

workflows.name: Phone handling
steps: Greet with the script; name the office and yourself
Verify identity before any account detail
Listen and restate the request before acting
Handle one request at a time; say which need someone else
Use only approved language ({APPROVED_PHRASES}); avoid {PROHIBITED_PHRASES}
Hold or transfer only with permission, per {HOLD_TRANSFER_RULE}
Follow {VOICEMAIL_RULE} on voicemails
Close with a summary of next steps; write the call note
workflows.definition_of_done: Caller's request handled or routed with an owner and time, approved language only, call note written.
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Admitting liability or fault
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; Module 4 three roleplays and Module 5 three capstones passed on the voice simulator.

workflows.name: Text responses
workflows.trigger: A patient or unknown number texts the office, or the VA sends a reminder.
steps: Check the channel and recipient are approved; verify the sender
Check for red flags first (urgent symptoms, clinical questions, complaints)
For admin requests covered by a template, verify details and reply with the template
Follow policy for insurance, billing, records, opt-outs ({OPT_OUT_RULE}) and after-hours ({AFTER_HOURS_RULE})
Reply within {TEXT_RESPONSE_TIME}
Document per {TEXT_DOC_RULE}
workflows.definition_of_done: Correct reply sent (or a deliberate pause and escalation), opt-outs honored, conversation documented.
requires_approval: Insurance guarantees, billing exceptions, records requests
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
common_mistakes: Sharing details with an unverified number
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Texting after an opt-out
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; Module 6 ten-text set 10/10.

workflows.name: EHR documentation
workflows.trigger: Any chart work: finding patients, new patient file setup, forms, uploads, notes setup, audits.
steps: Confirm the right patient before opening or editing
Search by more than name; never create a duplicate chart
Follow the New Patient Checklist in order; check and date each step
Upload only readable, complete documents to the right chart and category, named correctly
Route outside records per {RECORDS_ROUTING}; never interpret them
Fix mistakes through {CORRECTION_PROCESS}; never delete or hide them
Run the Day 6 audit per {Q_AUDIT_STEPS}
workflows.definition_of_done: Right chart, complete and readable documents, correct category and name, checklist steps dated, nothing hidden, audit gaps assigned.
va_can_decide: Requesting a clearer copy from a patient
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
Anything filed to the wrong patient: report the same day per {CORRECTION_PROCESS}
common_mistakes: Marking unsigned or partial forms complete
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Altering signatures or records
Writing clinical content in notes
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; 10 fake patients run through the New Patient Checklist with every step dated; vendor EHR training completed.

workflows.name: Insurance verification
workflows.trigger: A new patient with insurance is booked, a plan changes, or verification is due ({VERIFY_TIMING}).
required_information: Subscriber name, date of birth, relationship
steps: Confirm the right patient and policy
Collect insurer, plan, member ID, group, subscriber details; never assume the patient is the subscriber
Check eligibility in {ELIGIBILITY_SOURCE} for the date of service
Record every field in {VERIFICATION_FIELDS}, marking anything unavailable N/A with a reason
Record source, date and time, reference number and representative
Document in {INS_NOTE_LOCATION}
Tell the patient only verified facts using {NONGUARANTEE_SCRIPT}
workflows.definition_of_done: All required fields recorded or marked N/A with reason, source and reference captured, uncertainty escalated, no guarantee given.
va_can_decide: Marking fields N/A with a reason
common_mistakes: Recording only one of two conflicting results
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Fabricating payer results
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; Module 7 three mock verifications complete with every field.

workflows.name: Billing questions
workflows.trigger: A charge, payment, EOB, balance question or billing routine.
required_information: Verified identity for any account question
Ledger, payment system and (insurance offices) EOB
steps: Verify identity before discussing an account
Match patient, payer, date of service and claim before posting anything
Charge only the service and amount in {VISIT_PRICE_LIST}; send receipt; record in {CASH_LOG}
Reconcile totals between payment system, ledger and log
Post only what {BILLING_AUTHORITY} allows; escalate everything else to {BILLER}
Record every follow-up in {BILLING_LOG} with source, action, owner, next step, resolution
workflows.definition_of_done: Every amount matches, nothing posted outside authority, discrepancies escalated, follow-ups recorded and closed.
va_can_decide: Tasks {BILLING_AUTHORITY} lets the VA do alone
immediate_escalation: Wrong-patient posting or EOB: report per {CORRECTION_PROCESS} the same day
common_mistakes: Leaving recurring billing active after cancel
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Unauthorized refunds or write-offs
Writing down full card numbers
Changing codes
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; Module 8 six mock cases (or six cash cases) 6/6 with 100% correct math.

workflows.name: Patient escalation
workflows.trigger: A clinical question, possible emergency, complaint, privacy request, review or legal threat, or anything outside VA authority.
required_information: What the caller said, in their words
steps: Recognize the boundary: clinical, safety, privacy, legal, money or authority
For red flags, follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} word for word, immediately
Don't diagnose, reassure, interpret or promise
Route to the right owner through {ESCALATION_CHANNEL}, with a complete message
Tell the caller who will follow up and when
Document the exact words and every step with times
workflows.definition_of_done: Boundary recognized, correct owner notified in time, caller told the next step, exact words documented.
va_can_decide: Offering the soonest visit or callback
immediate_escalation: Caller or patient mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} or describes a possible emergency: follow {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} immediately
common_mistakes: Delaying an emergency to finish another task
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Admitting liability
Offering favors to change a review
workflows.pass_standard: 100% of red-flag scenarios routed correctly; 80% overall with zero critical errors.

workflows.name: Daily reporting
workflows.trigger: Start of day, end of day, handoffs, and team communication (Slack, email, remote access).
steps: Open the office ({REMOTE_ACCESS_TOOL} if used) and work {OPENING_TASKS} in order, same-day items first
Own every task to completion or hand it off with owner, status and due time
Use the right Slack channel with only what {PHI_CHANNEL_RULE} allows
Manage email per {EMAIL_LABELS} and {EMAIL_ROUTING}
Close with {CLOSING_TASKS}; carry unfinished tasks forward
Post the EOD report answering: what I worked on, what I'm stuck on, what I need
workflows.definition_of_done: Every task completed, handed off or carried forward with an owner; EOD report posted with real numbers and specific asks.
requires_approval: Anything blocked needing a decision: ask specifically
immediate_escalation: System outage at a critical time: tell {ESCALATION_CONTACT} by a backup method
prohibited_actions: Giving clinical or medical advice, or interpreting X-rays, imaging or results
Sharing patient information before verifying identity ({PATIENT_ID_CHECK})
Promising results, coverage, prices or exceptions the office hasn't approved
Marking work done that wasn't done
Sharing passwords or logins
workflows.pass_standard: 80% with zero critical errors; Module 9 simulated day with all tasks accounted for.

Which billing does the VA handle: insurance, cash, both, or none?
Do you have a re-exam checklist or card?
Are there extra office-specific tasks (gray cards) the VA must do?
Which apply: PIP/MVA, workers' comp, attorney record requests, Medicare? (each becomes a gray card)
What's the office name exactly as staff say it on the phone?
How should the VA refer to you with patients (Dr. Last name, first name)?
List every service you offer (adjustments, laser, decompression, massage, rehab, etc.).
What do patients ask for that you do NOT offer?
Your office mission in 1-2 sentences.
What makes your office different from the chiropractor down the street?
Your top 3 core values, each with one line on what it looks like in practice.
The exact greeting for phone calls and the first text to a new contact.
3 things the VA must always do.
default_answer: Verify identity before sharing any patient detail
Confirm every booking saved before telling the patient
Document every call, text and task in the chart or log

rule_slots.question: 3 things the VA must never do.
default_answer: Never give medical advice or interpret results
Never promise results, coverage or prices
Never mark a task done that isn't done

rule_slots.question: The mistakes past front desk staff made that you never want repeated.
default_answer: Booking the wrong visit type or length
Not booking the report of findings on the first call
Leaving tasks off the EOD report

rule_slots.question: Who does the VA go to when stuck, and who's the backup if they don't answer?
Where does the VA send questions (Slack channel, text) and how fast should they expect a reply?
rule_slots.default_answer: Post in the office's main Slack channel; expect a reply within 30 minutes during office hours. If urgent or no reply, text or call the escalation contact.

rule_slots.question: What exactly should the VA say and do if a caller describes an emergency?
rule_slots.default_answer: Say: "Based on what you're describing, please call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room now." Do not diagnose or reassure. Then alert the escalation contact immediately and document the time and the caller's exact words.

rule_slots.question: Office hours by day, and the VA's start and end time.
The VA's opening tasks, in order.
The VA's closing tasks, in order.
When and how are tomorrow's appointments confirmed (text, call, both; what time)?
rule_slots.default_answer: Confirm all of tomorrow's appointments by text the day before, by 3 p.m.; call anyone who hasn't confirmed by end of day.

rule_slots.question: How soon after a missed appointment does the VA reach out, and how?
rule_slots.default_answer: Call within 15 minutes of the missed time; if no answer, leave an approved voicemail and send a text. Offer to rebook. Flag a second miss to the escalation contact.

rule_slots.question: Where is the EOD report posted, and by what time?
rule_slots.default_answer: Post in Slack by the end of the VA's shift, answering: what I worked on today, what I'm having challenges with, what specifically I need help with.

rule_slots.question: Name each stage of your patient journey with the day it happens.
How many visits or days until a re-exam?
Which EHR do you use?
Where does the VA take the vendor's EHR training (link or platform)? What proves they finished it?
rule_slots.auto_rule: VFDA fills from its vendor training list for the office's EHR

rule_slots.question: Which 2 identifiers must the VA confirm before opening or editing a chart?
rule_slots.default_answer: Full name and date of birth

rule_slots.question: Who handles possible duplicate charts, and what does the VA do meanwhile?
rule_slots.default_answer: Don't merge or edit either chart. Flag it to the escalation contact with both chart names; keep working only on the verified chart.

rule_slots.question: What patient details may the VA post in Slack or screenshots?
rule_slots.default_answer: Patient initials or chart number only. No full names with clinical details, no diagnoses, no chart screenshots.

rule_slots.question: After a cancellation, what must the VA record and do?
rule_slots.default_answer: Record the reason, offer to rebook once, offer the slot to the waitlist, and note the outcome in the chart.

rule_slots.question: If something is entered or attached to the wrong chart, what's the correction and reporting process?
rule_slots.default_answer: Don't delete or hide it. Tell the escalation contact the same day, note what happened, and follow their correction. If another patient's information was exposed, treat it as a privacy incident.

rule_slots.question: List every form a new patient must complete before Visit 1.
Which document categories or folders do you use in the EHR?
How should uploaded files be named?
rule_slots.default_answer: LastName_FirstName_DocumentType_YYYY-MM-DD

rule_slots.question: When outside records, referrals or imaging reports arrive, who needs to be notified and how?
rule_slots.default_answer: Upload to the right chart and category, then message the doctor that it's there. Never read out or act on the content.

rule_slots.question: When there are duplicate or outdated documents, what's kept, and who approves removing anything?
rule_slots.default_answer: Keep both. Label the current one clearly; only the doctor or escalation contact may approve removing anything.

rule_slots.question: Which texting platform do you use?
Which phone system do you use?
Where does the VA take the texting platform's training? What proves they finished?
rule_slots.auto_rule: VFDA fills from its vendor training list for the texting platform

rule_slots.question: Where does the VA take the phone system's training? What proves they finished?
rule_slots.auto_rule: VFDA fills from its vendor training list for the phone system

rule_slots.question: Paste your approved texts for confirming, rescheduling and canceling.
How does the VA verify who's texting before sharing appointment details?
rule_slots.default_answer: Text is from the number on file; if not, ask for full name and date of birth before sharing anything.

rule_slots.question: Where is a patient's consent to receive texts recorded?
rule_slots.default_answer: Recorded on the intake form and noted in the chart.

rule_slots.question: What happens when a patient texts STOP or asks not to be texted?
rule_slots.default_answer: Stop all texts immediately, mark the patient opted out, and note it in the chart. Contact by phone only from then on.

rule_slots.question: How fast must texts be answered during office hours?
rule_slots.default_answer: Within 15 minutes during office hours.

rule_slots.question: What does the VA do with texts or calls that come in after hours?
rule_slots.default_answer: Send the approved after-hours reply; if the message mentions urgent symptoms, follow the emergency protocol. Handle everything else first thing next morning.

rule_slots.question: Where are texts and calls documented?
rule_slots.default_answer: Log every text and call in the patient's chart (EHR note).

rule_slots.question: Parking and directions, as you want them texted.
Who handles complaints, and how fast must the VA hand them off?
rule_slots.default_answer: Apologize, get the facts, offer a specific next step, and hand it to the escalation contact the same day.

rule_slots.question: What may the VA say on a patient's voicemail, and what must never be left?
rule_slots.default_answer: Leave only your first name, the office name and a callback number. Never leave appointment details, balances or reasons for visit.

rule_slots.question: Who can calls be transferred to, and what happens if they don't pick up?
rule_slots.default_answer: Ask permission before holding. Transfer only to the person the caller needs; if they don't answer, return to the caller and take a message.

rule_slots.question: How fast must missed calls and voicemails be returned?
rule_slots.default_answer: Same business day, within 2 hours.

rule_slots.question: Scheduling Rules Matrix: one row per visit type with duration, provider, allowed times, buffer, double-book rule, approval owner, escalation, documentation.
How is a care plan booked? Visits per week by phase, and how many visits ahead the VA books.
How soon after Day 1 must the report of findings be booked, and in which time blocks?
Which blocks can never be booked (lunch, admin, doctor-only time)?
Which providers see which visit types? Any patient restrictions?
Until what time can same-day appointments be booked, and who approves after that?
rule_slots.default_answer: Same-day bookings allowed until 2 hours before close; after that, the doctor approves.

rule_slots.question: What counts as an urgent scheduling request, and who decides if they're squeezed in?
rule_slots.default_answer: Urgent = new or worse pain that can't wait. Escalate to the doctor; the doctor decides on a squeeze-in. Red-flag symptoms follow the emergency protocol.

rule_slots.question: What's a late cancellation (how many hours), and what happens?
How is the waitlist kept, and who gets offered an open slot first?
rule_slots.default_answer: Keep the waitlist in the EHR; offer open slots in the order people joined, only if the slot fits their visit type and length.

rule_slots.question: Who can approve exceptions to scheduling rules, and how must the approval be recorded?
rule_slots.default_answer: The doctor. The approval is noted on the appointment with who approved it and when.

rule_slots.question: Should visits be grouped to avoid gaps in the doctor's day? What's the rule?
rule_slots.default_answer: Group visits to avoid gaps in the doctor's day; offer gap times first.

rule_slots.question: Here are our 6 'before patient arrival' steps. Which do you use, in what order, and what would you add?
Where do new patient intake forms come in?
Which patient details are entered before arrival, and which at check-in?
rule_slots.default_answer: Enter all intake details before arrival; confirm date of birth and contact details at check-in.

rule_slots.question: Do you use a separate X-ray or scan system that needs a patient profile before Day 1? Which one?
What must be printed or prepared for the onsite team before the patient arrives?
rule_slots.default_answer: Intake paperwork and the consult/exam form, ready before the patient arrives.

rule_slots.question: List each code you use on the schedule and what it means.
Do you hold a daily huddle? What must the VA report about each Day 1?
rule_slots.default_answer: Daily huddle: for each Day 1, report whether Day 0 is complete, the type of Day 1, and anything missing with who will fix it.

rule_slots.question: What types of Day 1 visits do you have?
Walk us through check-in at the front desk, step by step.
Which visit or transaction code is entered for a new patient exam, and when?
Which system takes payments, and what is charged on Day 1?
After Day 1, which scans or files go into the chart, and which exactly does the doctor need?
Do you collect insurance cards on Day 1? If yes, how?
What does the VA do before, during and after the report of findings visit?

What does the Day 6 Q audit check, and who fixes each kind of gap?

Report of findings booked or done

rule_slots.question: How are upcoming re-exams spotted?
What does the VA prepare before a re-exam?
When is the 'view' visit booked after a re-exam, and how long is it?
When a care plan ends, what's the VA's part in the re-sign process?
Upload your inbound phone script (new patient, existing patient, confirmation).
Upload your outbound script (reminders, no-shows, reactivation).
Which questions must be asked on every new patient call, and which are optional?
default_answer: What brings them in (in their words)

rule_slots.question: What can the VA say about prices on the phone? Who handles discounts?
When a caller asks about a policy that isn't written down, what should the VA say and who do they ask?
rule_slots.default_answer: Say: "Let me check that for you and call you back by [time]." Ask the escalation contact, call back, and note the answer so it can be added to the SOP.

rule_slots.question: What goes in a call note, and where in the EHR?
rule_slots.default_answer: Date, reason for the call, what was done, what's still open and who owns it, in the patient's chart.

rule_slots.question: List your Slack channels and what each one is for.
Which email inbox does the VA manage?
Which labels or folders do you use?
Which kinds of email must be passed to you or the team, and how fast?
rule_slots.default_answer: Records requests, legal or attorney letters, billing issues and anything needing a signature go to the doctor or team the same day.

rule_slots.question: When an email needs a signature, where does the signed scan go?
rule_slots.default_answer: The office's shared Google Drive folder for signed documents.

rule_slots.question: Do you use remote desktop access (e.g. ConnectWise)? Which tool?
Which office computers does the VA connect to, and in what order?
Do you have a script for cost or 'I'll think about it' objections? Upload it.
rule_slots.default_answer: Acknowledge the concern, explain what the first visit includes, offer the next available time, and offer to have the doctor's team follow up. No discounts unless approved.

rule_slots.question: Which phrases should the VA use to calm an upset caller?
default_answer: I understand, and I'm sorry for the frustration.
Let me make sure I have this right.
Here's what I can do right now.
I'll make sure the right person follows up by [time].

rule_slots.question: What must the VA never say or promise?
What can the VA decide alone, and what always needs you?
rule_slots.default_answer: The VA may offer any open slot within the scheduling rules, add to the waitlist, resend forms and confirmations, and answer approved FAQ. Everything involving money, exceptions, clinical questions or complaints goes to the escalation contact.

rule_slots.question: Who handles billing disputes, refund requests and chargeback threats? How fast?
rule_slots.default_answer: Take the details and send to the biller or doctor the same day; tell the patient who will follow up and when. No refunds or adjustments by the VA.

rule_slots.question: When a caller demands to speak to the doctor right now, what's the VA's path?
rule_slots.default_answer: Explain the doctor is with patients, check for red flags, take a complete message and send it to the doctor; tell the caller when to expect a reply.

rule_slots.question: Where are a patient's approved contacts recorded?
rule_slots.default_answer: Listed on the intake form and in the chart's contacts section.

rule_slots.question: What does the VA do when a caller threatens or mentions a bad online review?
rule_slots.default_answer: Stay calm, solve the problem if possible, and tell the escalation contact the same day. Never offer anything in exchange for changing a review.

rule_slots.question: What does the VA do when a caller mentions a lawyer, complaint board or liability?
rule_slots.default_answer: Stay neutral, don't admit or deny anything, write down the caller's exact words, and tell the doctor immediately.

rule_slots.question: Which words or symptoms should make the VA follow the emergency protocol immediately?
default_answer: Loss of bladder or bowel control
New numbness or weakness in arms or legs
Severe pain after a fall or accident

rule_slots.question: Which insurance plans are you in network with? Any you don't take?
How are insurance cards collected? Front and back?
rule_slots.default_answer: Front and back photo or scan, uploaded to the chart before Day 1.

rule_slots.question: Where does the VA check eligibility?
When is insurance verified?
rule_slots.default_answer: Before Day 1, every January, and whenever the patient says their plan changed.

rule_slots.question: Module 7's list of fields to record: which do you require, and which are optional?
Where in the EHR is the verification documented?
rule_slots.default_answer: Insurance section of the patient's chart, as a dated note.

rule_slots.question: Exact words the VA should use when a patient asks if a visit is covered.
rule_slots.default_answer: "Your plan shows [benefits as reported]. That's what your insurance told us today; the final amount depends on how they process the claim."

rule_slots.question: What happens when coverage is inactive, terminated or not yet active?
rule_slots.default_answer: Tell the patient neutrally, ask for a new card, offer self-pay or rescheduling, and flag it at the huddle.

rule_slots.question: What happens with out-of-network patients?
rule_slots.default_answer: Explain neutrally that the office is out of network for their plan, share the self-pay option, and note it in the chart.

rule_slots.question: Which plans need a referral or authorization, and who gets it?
rule_slots.default_answer: If the plan may need a referral or authorization, record what's uncertain, escalate to the insurance escalation owner, and don't tell the patient they're covered until it's resolved.

rule_slots.question: Who handles conflicting or unclear insurance information? How fast?
rule_slots.default_answer: The biller or doctor, the same day.

rule_slots.question: Who owns billing, and who does the VA hand billing issues to?
What may the VA post alone, and what always needs approval (write-offs, refunds, adjustments)?
rule_slots.default_answer: The VA may post patient payments and approved contractual adjustments. Write-offs, refunds and any other adjustment need the doctor's approval.

rule_slots.question: How and when do patients get their statements from the office?
rule_slots.default_answer: Statements are sent monthly by the office; the VA explains that any balance owed will be on that statement.

rule_slots.question: Any rounding rule for balances?
rule_slots.default_answer: No rounding; use exact amounts.

rule_slots.question: Where are billing follow-ups recorded?
rule_slots.default_answer: A dated note in the patient's ledger or the office's billing log.

rule_slots.question: Is there a set billing day or routine the VA follows?
Where do EOBs come in?
rule_slots.default_answer: Payer portal or mailed EOBs scanned to the office's billing folder.

rule_slots.question: How long before a pending or unpaid claim gets followed up?
rule_slots.default_answer: 30 days with no payment or decision.

rule_slots.question: Who is charged at each visit, who's on a recurring plan, and who pays up front?
Which service or code is entered for each visit type, and at what price?
Where else is each payment recorded?
rule_slots.default_answer: The office's daily collections log.

rule_slots.question: What does the VA do when a card is declined?
rule_slots.default_answer: Tell the patient discreetly, ask for another payment method, never charge another card without consent, and flag unpaid balances.

rule_slots.question: How are recurring plans set up and canceled, and what signed authorization is needed?
rule_slots.default_answer: Recurring billing only with a signed authorization on file. Set the exact amount, start date and frequency. Stop it the same day a plan is canceled and confirm no future charges are scheduled.

rule_slots.question: When can the VA send a payment link, and how is it confirmed?
rule_slots.default_answer: Send a payment link only to the verified email or phone on file, for the exact balance, and confirm it's paid before closing the task.

rule_slots.question: Team members (name, role, who the VA goes to for what)
Approved tools (texting, phone, payments, insurance portal, Slack, email, remote access)
General preferences (tone, what the doctor cares about most)

schedule.title: EHR Training
proof_of_work: Completion proof from the vendor EHR training at {EHR_TRAINING_LINK}
3 screenshots from {EHR_NAME}, fake patients only: a patient search, an upcoming appointment, and an uploaded, correctly named document
schedule.notes: Scoring for situational: 2 = right action and right approach and steps per the office's rules, 1 = right action but a missed or out-of-order step, 0 = wrong action.

schedule.title: Texting / VOIP
proof_of_work: Completion proof from both platform trainings ({TEXT_TRAINING_LINK}, {VOIP_TRAINING_LINK})

Module 6 10-text set: 10 sample replies to a fake patient (confirm, unavailable slot, office hours, missed callback, X-ray question, urgent symptoms, unknown number, STOP, insurance guarantee or a replacement for cash offices, cancellation). All 10 must be correct.

schedule.title: Scheduling Cadence
proof_of_work: Module 3 10-sample assessment, booked in {EHR_NAME} with fake patients and screenshotted. Pass = 9/10: new patient slot too short; routine follow-up; reschedule without duplicate; late cancellation; urgent request requiring escalation; protected buffer conflict; unapproved double-book; wrong provider; same-day request after cutoff; doctor-approved exception.
schedule.notes: Every situational answer is checked against M3's Verify list: type, length, provider, buffer, double-booking, approval, documentation, escalation. Any one missed on a booking caps that item at 1.

schedule.title: New Patient & Re-exam Checklists
proof_of_work: The 10 fake patients built in {EHR_NAME} and Trello, each run through the office's New Patient Checklist from Day 0 to Day 6 with every step checked and dated. VFDA spot-checks 3 against {Q_AUDIT_STEPS}.
schedule.notes: Order matters: a step done out of order, or not dated, caps that item at 1 point. Offices without a re-exam card get Part B-alt instead of Part B.

schedule.title: Basic Phone Handling
cards: How To: Open Office with ConnectWise
proof_of_work: Module 4's three required roleplays on the voice call simulator with the office's script loaded: new patient first appointment; existing patient routine scheduling or account question; appointment confirmation. All three must pass.
schedule.notes: Say part graded on M4 checklist: greeting, identity, required questions, approved language, documentation, closing, escalation. Situational: 2 = Say, Do and Book all right; 1 = one part wrong or missing; 0 = two or more wrong. Offices without remote access skip B3 and get a second Email item.

schedule.title: Challenging Phone Handling
proof_of_work: Module 5's three capstone roleplays on the voice simulator: financial objection; upset scheduling patient; safety/privacy/escalation. All three must pass with no unresolved critical error.
VA-written Challenging Call Script & Escalation Checklist, submitted in Slack and approved by the doctor.
schedule.notes: Say part graded on M5 checklist: calm tone, listening/empathy, clarifying questions, approved language, boundaries, escalation, objective notes, closing.

schedule.title: Insurance
proof_of_work: Module 7's three mock verifications (A active, B inactive/terminated/not yet effective, C conflicting or authorization uncertainty), each with every field in {VERIFICATION_FIELDS} recorded or marked N/A with reason, correct escalation, no guarantee of payment.
VA-written Insurance Verification Checklist, approved by the doctor.
schedule.notes: Graded on M7 checklist: accuracy, source, documentation, limits of authority, uncertainty, escalation. Never fabricate unavailable data. Cash-only offices get 20 extra phone drills instead.

schedule.title: Billing
proof_of_work: Insurance track: Module 8's six mock EOB cases on its Mock Case Record, 6/6 with 100% matching and math.
Cash track: six mock cash cases (paid visit reconciled; recurring plan set up; declined card; end-of-day mismatch; duplicate or wrong-patient charge; refund request escalated), 6/6.
VA-written Basic Billing Checklist, approved by the doctor.
schedule.notes: Tracks: billing_type insurance -> Parts A+B; cash -> Parts C+D; both -> Parts A+C. Any math error on a reconciliation item scores 0. Mark missing EOB fields 'not shown'.

schedule.title: Combined Gray Cards
proof_of_work: For each gray card: one demonstration on fake data (screenshots or Loom) start to finish, plus the record from {CARD_DONE}. VFDA checks high-risk cards first.
schedule.notes: Built per office from gray cards using GRAY_FORMULAS and GRAY_SPLIT. Pass = 80% of total points with zero critical errors; review 65-79%; below 65% retake.

scenarios.stem: What is a subluxation?
options: A torn muscle in the back
A vertebra out of proper alignment that interferes with the nervous system
A small fracture in the spine

scenarios.stem: A new patient asks what an adjustment is. Which answer is best?
options: "The doctor cracks your back to put the bones back in place."
"It's a precise, controlled movement the doctor applies to a specific area of the spine to help it move better. The doctor will explain more at your visit."
"It fixes whatever is causing your pain in one visit."

scenarios.stem: Which of these does {CLINIC_NAME} NOT offer?
scenarios.options_rule: Three items from {SERVICES} and one from {NOT_OFFERED}, in random order

scenarios.stem: What does "wellness care" mean?
options: Care only for patients who are in pain
Regular adjustments to maintain spinal health after the pain is gone

scenarios.stem: What is the VA's role in patient education?
options: Help patients understand their schedule and care plan logistics, and send clinical questions to the doctor
Decide how often the patient should come in

scenarios.stem: A new caller says: "My neck has hurt for a week and now my arm tingles. Is this a pinched nerve? Should I be worried?" What do you say and do?
scenarios.critical_fail: "It sounds like a pinched nerve," "That's nothing to worry about," or any diagnosis
correct_response: acknowledges the pain with empathy
does not diagnose or say whether it's serious
explains {DOCTOR_NAME} will evaluate it at the first visit
offers the first available new patient appointment
asks if symptoms are sudden or severe, and follows {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} if so

scenarios.stem: A caller asks: "Do you do {NOT_OFFERED_ITEM}? And what's {SERVICE_ITEM}?" What do you say?
scenarios.critical_fail: claiming the office offers something it doesn't, or promising a result
correct_response: answers honestly that {NOT_OFFERED_ITEM} isn't offered
describes {SERVICE_ITEM} in one or two plain sentences
no promised results
offers a visit so the doctor can recommend what fits

scenarios.stem: A patient on a care plan says: "I feel fine now. Do I really need to keep coming?" What do you say and do?
scenarios.critical_fail: promising an outcome ("If you finish, it won't come back")
correct_response: acknowledges the progress
explains in general terms why care plans continue past pain relief
does not change or cancel the plan on their own
offers to have {DOCTOR_NAME} go over it at the next visit
notes it in the chart or flags it to {ESCALATION_CONTACT}

scenarios.stem: Which statement is {CLINIC_NAME}'s mission?
scenarios.options_rule: {OFFICE_MISSION} plus three realistic decoys written from other offices' missions

scenarios.stem: How do you answer the phone at {CLINIC_NAME}?
You're stuck on a task and {ESCALATION_CONTACT} hasn't replied in the expected time. What do you do?
options: Contact the backup through {ESCALATION_CHANNEL}, move to other tasks, and list the blocker in your EOD report
Tell the patient to call back tomorrow

scenarios.stem: A caller asks: "Why should I come to you instead of the chiropractor near my house?" What do you say?
scenarios.critical_fail: promising results ("we'll fix it for sure")
correct_response: explains {OFFICE_USP} in their own words
connects it to what the caller needs
doesn't criticize other offices
no promised results
offers an appointment

scenarios.stem: Name the three things you must never do at {CLINIC_NAME}. For one of them, describe a real situation where you'd be tempted to do it, and what you'd do instead.
correct_response: all three match {DONTS}
the situation is realistic for a front desk
the alternative action is correct and within the VA's role

scenarios.stem: A patient calls, frustrated: "Nobody told me my first visit would take that long or what it would cost." Using {CLINIC_NAME}'s core values, how do you handle the call?
scenarios.critical_fail: quoting a price or policy the office hasn't approved
correct_response: apologizes without blaming other staff
shows at least one of {CORE_VALUES} through action, not just by naming it

documents the complaint

scenarios.stem: What's the first task on your opening list?
scenarios.options_rule: The first item of {OPENING_TASKS} plus three later items from the same list

scenarios.stem: When and how are tomorrow's appointments confirmed?
scenarios.options_rule: {CONFIRM_RULE} plus three wrong timings or methods

scenarios.stem: Which three questions does your EOD report answer?
options: How many calls, how many texts, how many bookings
What did you work on today, what are you having challenges with, what specifically do you need help with
What went well, what went badly, what's tomorrow's plan
Who called, who texted, who canceled

scenarios.stem: You log in to start your day. Waiting for you: 2 voicemails from last night, 1 new patient web lead, 4 unconfirmed appointments for today, and a text from your 9:00 patient: "running 10 min late." In what order do you handle these, and why?
correct_response: handles same-day, time-sensitive items first (the late 9:00 patient, voicemails that may be today's cancellations)
contacts the new lead fast
confirms today's unconfirmed appointments before they arrive

scenarios.stem: Your 10:00 patient hasn't shown up. It's 10:20. Walk through exactly what you do.
correct_response: checks {EHR_NAME} that the patient wasn't checked in, rescheduled or canceled
marks the correct status
reaches out per {NO_SHOW_RULE}
offers to reschedule
records the outcome

records both attempts and times

scenarios.stem: Write your EOD report for this mock day: 18 confirmations sent, 2 no-shows (reached 1, rebooked 1), 1 new patient booked, the fax system wouldn't log in, and a patient asked for a Saturday appointment, which you're not sure is allowed.

The visit where the doctor explains the exam results and recommends a care plan
The patient's last visit before discharge
A phone call from the VA with the patient's results

scenarios.options_rule: {REEXAM_INTERVAL} plus three wrong intervals

scenarios.stem: A patient who had their first exam yesterday calls: "Did my X-rays show anything? What's wrong with me?" What do you say and do?
scenarios.critical_fail: sharing, guessing or interpreting any result

scenarios.stem: A new patient just booked their first visit for tomorrow. List everything you do between now and when they walk in.
correct_response: follows the Day 0 stage of {JOURNEY_STAGES}
sets up the chart in {EHR_NAME}

scenarios.stem: Before opening or editing a patient's chart, what must you confirm?
options: Nothing, if the name matches exactly

scenarios.stem: You're checking a patient's next appointment. Which details do you confirm?
options: Date, time, provider, location and appointment type

scenarios.stem: You just booked an appointment. How do you know it was saved?
options: The screen didn't show an error
You reopen the schedule or chart and see it there before confirming with the patient
The patient got a confirmation text

scenarios.stem: What patient details may you share in Slack or a screenshot?
options: A full chart screenshot so the doctor sees everything
Only what {PHI_CHANNEL_RULE} allows, with no clinical details
Full name and reason for visit

scenarios.stem: A caller named Sam Rivera wants to book, but searching by name in {EHR_NAME} shows no results. What do you do?
correct_response: searches using other identifiers (date of birth, phone, other spellings)
confirms spelling and date of birth with the caller
doesn't create a new chart until sure there isn't one
if truly new, starts the new patient process
notes what was searched

scenarios.critical_fail: merging or editing either chart, or reading the other chart's details to the caller
correct_response: verifies identity with {PATIENT_ID_CHECK} plus phone or address
doesn't merge, edit or guess

moves only the verified appointment and rechecks it saved

scenarios.stem: You moved a patient's Tuesday 10:00 visit to Thursday 2:00. When you check the calendar, the patient now shows on both days.
correct_response: notices the duplicate before confirming with the patient
removes the old Tuesday slot through the reschedule or cancel step, not by deleting entries
rechecks that only Thursday remains
then confirms with the patient

scenarios.stem: A patient calls to cancel tomorrow's visit and doesn't want to rebook right now.
scenarios.critical_fail: quoting a fee or policy the office hasn't set
correct_response: cancels with the correct status and reason
offers to rebook once, politely
follows {CANCEL_FOLLOWUP} for notes and follow-up
doesn't invent a cancellation fee or policy
confirms the slot is now open

scenarios.stem: The EHR freezes while you're booking. When it comes back, you're not sure the appointment saved.
scenarios.critical_fail: confirming an appointment that wasn't verified
correct_response: doesn't tell the patient it's booked until verified
reopens the schedule and the chart to check
checks for a half-saved or duplicate entry
rebooks if missing
reports the issue to {ESCALATION_CONTACT} if it repeats

scenarios.stem: You just saved a scheduling note and realize it's in the wrong patient's chart.
scenarios.critical_fail: deleting it quietly or not reporting it
correct_response: stops
doesn't delete or hide it
follows {CORRECTION_PROCESS}
tells {ESCALATION_CONTACT}
adds the note to the correct chart
rechecks both charts

scenarios.stem: Which forms must a new patient complete before Visit 1 at {CLINIC_NAME}?
scenarios.options_rule: {INTAKE_FORMS} plus three wrong combinations (one missing a form, one with a form the office doesn't use)

scenarios.stem: When is a document upload finished?
options: When the patient says they sent it
When it's saved, readable, in the right chart and category, named correctly, and sent to whoever needs to see it
When it appears anywhere in the EHR

scenarios.stem: Before attaching an outside imaging report, what do you check?
options: That the patient name, date of birth and study date match the chart
What the report says about the patient's condition
Nothing, if the patient sent it themselves

scenarios.stem: How do you name an uploaded document at {CLINIC_NAME}?

scenarios.critical_fail: marking an unsigned form complete or adding a signature
correct_response: doesn't mark either form complete
doesn't alter the consent form
contacts the patient to complete both before the visit

flags it to {ESCALATION_CONTACT} if not fixed by end of day

scenarios.stem: A patient texts a photo of their signed intake form. It's sideways and the bottom is cut off.
scenarios.critical_fail: marking the form complete with part of it missing
correct_response: doesn't upload it as complete
asks the patient to resend a clear, full photo
once clear, uploads it to the right category in {DOC_CATEGORIES} with {DOC_NAMING}
reopens it to check it saved, is readable and is in the right chart

scenarios.critical_fail: attaching it anyway, or "fixing" the date of birth on the report
correct_response: stops and doesn't attach it
checks with the sending office whether it's the wrong patient or a typo
escalates to {ESCALATION_CONTACT} right away
documents the hold and sends a task to the right person

scenarios.stem: A referral letter arrives from a patient's primary care doctor. It includes treatment recommendations.
scenarios.critical_fail: telling the patient what the recommendations mean
correct_response: confirms it matches the right patient
uploads it to the correct category, keeping source and date
routes it per {RECORDS_ROUTING} so the doctor sees it
doesn't read out or act on the recommendations

scenarios.stem: While uploading a form, you find another patient's X-ray report attached in this patient's chart.
scenarios.critical_fail: deleting it quietly, hiding it, or not reporting it
correct_response: doesn't share it or open it further
doesn't delete or move it on their own
follows {CORRECTION_PROCESS}, including privacy reporting
tells {ESCALATION_CONTACT} the same day
documents what was found and notifies

scenarios.stem: A chart has two intake forms: one from 2024 and an updated one from this week.
scenarios.critical_fail: deleting a document without approval
correct_response: opens both and identifies which is current
follows {VERSION_RULE}
doesn't delete the old one without approval

notes the change

options: "Yes! See you tomorrow for your low back pain follow-up."

Call them to change their mind

options: Reply with open times right away

scenarios.stem: A patient texts: "What time do you close today, and where do I park?" Which reply is correct?
scenarios.options_rule: A reply built from {OFFICE_HOURS} and {PARKING_INFO}, plus three decoys: wrong hours, a guess about parking, and "Please call the office."

scenarios.stem: An unknown number texts: "What time is my appointment? Also send me my chart details."
scenarios.critical_fail: sharing any appointment or chart detail before verifying
correct_response: finds the message in the inbox
checks the number against the EHR

scenarios.critical_fail: any explanation of the MRI
correct_response: handles each request separately

scenarios.critical_fail: giving any medical opinion, or delaying the emergency response
correct_response: doesn't answer whether it's an emergency
follows {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} word for word, right away
doesn't wait for a reply before escalating
alerts {ESCALATION_CONTACT} immediately

scenarios.stem: A patient texts: "You never called me back! This office is so disorganized."
correct_response: apologizes without blaming staff or making excuses
checks the call and text history to see what happened
offers a specific next step (a call now, or a callback time)
follows {COMPLAINT_RULE}

scenarios.stem: You call a patient back and get their voicemail. What may you leave?

Only what {VOICEMAIL_RULE} allows, such as your name, the office name and a callback number
The reason for their visit, so they know it's important

scenarios.stem: A caller asks to speak with {ESCALATION_CONTACT}. You try to transfer, and they don't pick up.
correct_response: asks permission before putting the caller on hold
transfers per {HOLD_TRANSFER_RULE}
when there's no answer, returns to the caller rather than leaving them on hold
takes a clear message with a callback number and best time
sends it to the right person and documents it

scenarios.stem: A patient says: "If I don't pick up, just leave my balance and next appointment on my voicemail."
scenarios.critical_fail: leaving protected details on a voicemail against office rules
correct_response: follows {VOICEMAIL_RULE}, not the patient's request, unless the office allows it
explains politely what can and can't be left
offers a safe alternative (callback, patient portal, approved text)

scenarios.stem: You log in for the day. The phone system shows 3 missed calls and 2 voicemails from overnight.
scenarios.critical_fail: missing an urgent voicemail
correct_response: sets their phone status to available
checks missed calls and listens to every voicemail
matches each to a patient in the EHR
returns them within {CALLBACK_TIME}, urgent and same-day ones first
writes short, accurate call notes per {TEXT_DOC_RULE}
marks each one handled

scenarios.stem: At {CLINIC_NAME}, how long is a new patient visit and who sees the patient?
scenarios.options_rule: The duration and provider from {MATRIX_NEW_PATIENT}, plus three decoys taken from the other matrix rows

scenarios.stem: When must the report of findings be booked?
scenarios.options_rule: {ROF_RULE} plus three wrong timings (same day, "whenever the patient wants," a week later)

scenarios.stem: A new patient wants the last slot of the day. The opening is 30 minutes before close, but a new patient visit is longer than that per {MATRIX_NEW_PATIENT}.
scenarios.critical_fail: booking the new patient into a slot that's too short
correct_response: recognizes the slot is too short
doesn't shorten the visit or run past close
offers the nearest openings that fit the full length, provider and allowed times
books using the new patient visit type
books the report of findings per {ROF_RULE} while on the call

scenarios.stem: An existing patient on a care plan calls to book next week.
correct_response: checks the care plan in the chart
books the number of visits per week required by {CARE_PLAN_CADENCE}, not just one
uses the follow-up visit type, length and provider from {MATRIX_FOLLOW_UP}
checks if a re-exam falls in that week
reads back all dates and times

scenarios.stem: After their report of findings, a patient accepts a care plan. The doctor asks you to book it.
correct_response: books the series per {CARE_PLAN_CADENCE}
checks each visit for conflicts, blocks and holidays
includes the re-exam at the right point with the re-exam visit type
gives the patient the full list
confirms all are saved

scenarios.stem: A patient asks to have their re-exam with a provider who, per {PROVIDER_RULES}, doesn't do re-exams.
scenarios.critical_fail: booking a restricted visit with the wrong provider
correct_response: explains politely that re-exams are done by the provider in {MATRIX_REEXAM}
offers that provider's openings
doesn't book the wrong provider to please the patient
escalates to {EXCEPTION_OWNER} if the patient insists
documents the request

scenarios.stem: A patient insists on a time that falls inside a protected block.
scenarios.critical_fail: booking into a protected block without approval
correct_response: checks the schedule for {PROTECTED_BLOCKS}
doesn't book into the block
offers the closest allowed times
if the patient can't make any, offers the waitlist or escalates to {EXCEPTION_OWNER}
documents it

scenarios.stem: A patient wants 10:00 tomorrow, but that slot is already booked. They say, "Just squeeze me in, I'll be quick."
scenarios.critical_fail: double-booking without approval
correct_response: checks the matrix's double-book rule for that visit type
doesn't double-book unless the rule allows it
offers the nearest open times
offers the waitlist
escalates only if the rule says approval is possible

scenarios.stem: It's after {SAME_DAY_CUTOFF}. A patient asks to come in today.
scenarios.critical_fail: booking after the cutoff without approval
correct_response: knows the cutoff has passed
doesn't book on their own
checks if it's urgent per {URGENT_RULE}
asks the approver if the rule allows it, otherwise books the earliest next-day slot
documents it

scenarios.stem: An existing patient calls: "I hurt my back this morning and can barely move. Can I come in today?" The schedule is full.
scenarios.critical_fail: not escalating, or giving medical advice
correct_response: listens for emergency signs and follows {EMERGENCY_PROTOCOL} if any are present
doesn't give medical advice
follows {URGENT_RULE} and escalates to the decision-maker right away
tells the patient when they'll hear back
follows up and documents

scenarios.stem: A patient cancels 1 hour before their visit. What applies at {CLINIC_NAME}?
scenarios.options_rule: {LATE_CANCEL_RULE} plus three decoys: a made-up fee, "nothing, cancellations are free," and the wrong time window

scenarios.stem: A patient didn't come and didn't call. How do you record it?
A patient wants to move their re-exam to Friday. Friday only has short follow-up openings.
scenarios.critical_fail: changing the visit type to fit a slot
correct_response: keeps the re-exam visit type and length from {MATRIX_REEXAM}
doesn't turn it into a follow-up to make it fit
offers re-exam openings that fit
moves it
checks the old slot is cleared and there's no duplicate

scenarios.stem: A patient cancels 1 hour before their visit and gets upset when you mention the policy.
scenarios.critical_fail: waiving or inventing a fee without approval
correct_response: applies {LATE_CANCEL_RULE} exactly, no more and no less
stays calm and explains it once
doesn't waive or invent a fee
offers to rebook
escalates a waiver request to {EXCEPTION_OWNER}
cancels and the right reason

scenarios.stem: A patient cancels tomorrow at 10:00. Two people are on the waitlist.
correct_response: cancels with the correct reason and offers to rebook
checks the appointment in the EHR
offers the slot in the order set by {WAITLIST_RULE}
only books a waitlist patient if the slot fits their visit type and length
updates the waitlist and documents

scenarios.stem: A care plan patient has missed two visits in a row.
correct_response: marks today's miss
reaches out per {NO_SHOW_RULE}
offers to rebook and keep the care plan on track
flags the repeat misses to {ESCALATION_CONTACT}
documents each attempt

scenarios.stem: While reviewing tomorrow, you see two patients booked in the same 9:00 slot, and a 90-minute gap in the doctor's afternoon.
scenarios.critical_fail: canceling or moving a patient without telling them
correct_response: checks if the double-booking was approved per the matrix
if not, contacts one patient to move them, starting with the most recently booked or as the office decides
doesn't cancel anyone without contacting them
uses {SCHEDULE_GAP_RULE} to suggest filling the gap (waitlist, moving willing patients)
reports what was found and fixed

scenarios.stem: The doctor messages you: "Squeeze John in at 12:15 today," which is during lunch.
correct_response: confirms the approval comes from {EXCEPTION_OWNER} in an approved channel
books it
notes the approval (who, when) on the appointment as {EXCEPTION_OWNER} requires
treats it as a one-time exception, not a new rule

scenarios.stem: A patient halfway through a care plan says: "I'm on vacation for 3 weeks. Just push all my visits back."
scenarios.critical_fail: changing care plan frequency on their own
correct_response: doesn't just move every visit
explains in plain words that the doctor set the visit frequency
offers to fit visits before they leave if possible
asks {EXCEPTION_OWNER} how to rebuild the plan after they return
rebooks once approved
documents it

scenarios.stem: You just booked a new patient's first visit by phone. What's your final confirmation before ending the call?
scenarios.critical_fail: confirming before checking it saved
correct_response: reads back date, time, provider, location and visit type
tells them how long the visit takes and what to bring
checks the booking saved
sends the confirmation per {CONFIRM_RULE}
documents it

scenarios.stem: The routing form says each step is "checked and dated before moving on to the next step." What does that mean for you?
options: Check everything off at the end of the day
Finish and date each step in order, and don't start the next one until the current one is done
Only date the steps the doctor asks about
Skip steps that don't apply without noting why

scenarios.stem: Which list shows {CLINIC_NAME}'s Day 0 steps in the right order?
scenarios.options_rule: {DAY0_STEPS} in order, plus three versions with steps swapped or missing

scenarios.stem: On tomorrow's schedule you see the code "{CODE_X}." What does it mean?
scenarios.options_rule: The meaning of {CODE_X} from {CALENDAR_CODES}, plus the meanings of three other codes

scenarios.stem: When is a new patient's file created at {CLINIC_NAME}?
At the out-desk after Day 1, what must be booked before the patient leaves?
A new patient is booked for 9:00 tomorrow. Their intake forms came in through {INTAKE_PLATFORM}, but two sections are blank and there's no signature.
scenarios.critical_fail: checking off the intake step with forms incomplete
correct_response: pulls the forms
checks them against {INTAKE_FORMS}
doesn't check off the Day 0 step
contacts the patient today to finish and sign
if still missing by close, notes it for the onsite team and flags it at the huddle

scenarios.stem: Walk through every Day 0 step for a new patient booked tomorrow, in order, with where you click.
correct_response: follows {DAY0_STEPS} in order
creates the file
enters only the details {DEMOGRAPHICS_RULE} allows before arrival
sets up the {IMAGING_SYSTEM} profile if the office uses one
prepares {PRINT_PACKET}
checks and dates each step

scenarios.stem: It's the morning huddle. You have two Day 1 patients today. What do you report?
scenarios.critical_fail: reporting Day 0 complete when it isn't
correct_response: follows {HUDDLE_RULE}
confirms whether each patient's Day 0 list is complete
names the type of Day 1 from {DAY1_TYPES}
calls out anything missing (forms, signature, insurance card if applicable) and who will fix it

scenarios.stem: Your new patient has just arrived. Walk through the in-desk steps until they go to the doctor.
scenarios.critical_fail: entering the wrong code without flagging it
correct_response: follows {ARRIVAL_STEPS} in order
completes any details held back by {DEMOGRAPHICS_RULE}
enters {DAY1_CODES}
collects the insurance card only if the office uses the insurance add-on
passes the patient to the doctor

scenarios.stem: The patient comes back from the doctor. While you're booking the report of findings, they say: "I'll call later to schedule the results visit."
scenarios.critical_fail: sharing any exam findings to convince them
correct_response: explains in plain words that the results visit is when the doctor goes over what they found
offers specific times per {ROF_RULE}
books
charges Day 1 per {PAYMENT_SYSTEM}
if they still won't book, documents it and flags it to the doctor the same day

scenarios.stem: After Day 1, the patient's scans are ready. What do you upload?
scenarios.critical_fail: attaching a file to the wrong patient
correct_response: uploads only the files in {AFTER_DAY1_UPLOADS}
uploads them to the right category with {DOC_NAMING}
checks the patient name and date on each file first
reopens them to confirm they're readable
checks and dates the step

scenarios.stem: It's Day 2. What do you do before, during and after the report of findings?
correct_response: follows {DAY2_STEPS} in order
has everything ready before the patient arrives
if the patient accepts care, books the plan per {CARE_PLAN_CADENCE}
checks and dates each step

scenarios.stem: On Day 2, before seeing the doctor, the patient asks you: "What did the X-rays show? Do I really need all those visits?"
scenarios.critical_fail: any comment on findings or on whether they need care
correct_response: doesn't share or guess findings
doesn't comment on the number of visits
says the doctor will go over everything in a few minutes
tells the doctor the patient has these questions

scenarios.stem: It's Day 4 Homecare. The patient texts: "Which stretch should I do when it hurts?"
scenarios.critical_fail: giving exercise or pain advice
correct_response: completes {HOMECARE_STEPS}
doesn't recommend any stretch or exercise
points them to the homecare the doctor already gave, or offers to pass the question to the doctor
documents and flags it

scenarios.critical_fail: marking the audit complete with open gaps, or entering a charge without confirming what was paid
correct_response: works through {Q_AUDIT_STEPS} item by item
fixes what's the VA's to fix (dates the step after confirming it happened)
escalates the missing charge to whoever {Q_AUDIT_STEPS} names
doesn't mark the audit complete until every gap is fixed or assigned

scenarios.options_rule: {REEXAM_INTERVAL} plus three wrong visit numbers

scenarios.stem: What is the purpose of a re-exam?
options: To collect payment for the next phase
To update the patient on their care, home care, and further recommendations or services
A routine adjustment with a different name

scenarios.stem: At the morning huddle you notice a patient on today's schedule is at their re-exam visit, but they're booked as a regular adjustment.
scenarios.bank_ref: Re-exam 1, picked up on daily huddle
correct_response: spots it using {REEXAM_PICKUP}
tells the doctor at the huddle

explains that the doctor goes over the results at the view visit

prepares whatever paperwork the office uses
books the new plan per {CARE_PLAN_CADENCE}

scenarios.stem: What is charged on Day 1 at {CLINIC_NAME}?

scenarios.part_title: Extra new patient items (no re-exam card)
scenarios.stem: A Day 1 patient cancels the night before. What happens to their Day 0 work and checklist?

correct_response: deletes spam, promotions and social emails
files fax confirmations under the right label from {EMAIL_LABELS}
passes the records request to the doctor or team per {EMAIL_ROUTING}

scenarios.stem: Before discussing an existing patient's account or appointments, what do you confirm?

scenarios.stem: Which questions must you ask on every new patient call?
scenarios.options_rule: {NP_CALL_QUESTIONS} plus three decoys: one missing a required question, one adding detailed medical history, one adding questions the office doesn't use

scenarios.part_title: Standard calls with EHR and scheduling
scenarios.stem: What does every call close include?
options: A summary of next steps, a check that the caller understood, and the closing line from the script
A reminder of the cancellation fee

scenarios.stem: An existing patient calls to book their next visits.

scenarios.stem: An existing patient wants to change their visit to a different service.

scenarios.stem: A caller asks, "What time is my appointment Thursday?" before you've verified who they are.

scenarios.stem: A patient asks to move Tuesday to Wednesday, then halfway through says, "Actually, make it Friday."

scenarios.stem: A caller wants to reschedule, ask about their balance, and get a work note, all in one call.

Say: handles them one at a time
says which ones need someone else

routes the work note request per office rules

scenarios.part_title: Standard calls with EHR and scheduling
scenarios.stem: A caller asks about a policy that isn't in the SOP (e.g. "Can my teenager come in without me?").

scenarios.part_title: Standard calls with EHR and scheduling
scenarios.stem: A new caller asks how much the first visit costs and whether there's a discount.
scenarios.critical_fail: quoting a price or discount the office hasn't approved

Book: continues to book if the caller is ready

scenarios.part_title: Standard calls with EHR and scheduling
scenarios.stem: The call drops before you finish collecting a new patient's details.

scenarios.stem: Outbound: you're calling to confirm tomorrow's appointments. One patient says they need a different time.

correct_response: logs in with their own credentials
checks email for the one-time code
opens {REMOTE_DESKTOPS} in order

prints it or sends it for signature as the office does it
asks for the signed copy to be scanned into {SIGNED_DOCS_FOLDER}

correct_response: right channel from {SLACK_CHANNELS}
patient identified only as {PHI_CHANNEL_RULE} allows
one specific question the doctor can answer yes or no

Do: asks {EXCEPTION_OWNER} only if the rule allows it

scenarios.stem: A patient says the office booked the wrong appointment, and that a promised callback never happened.

A caller who mentions any of {RED_FLAGS} while complaining about something else
A caller threatening a bad review
A patient asking to speak to the doctor about their care plan

loop: Ask the VA: show me how you do this
VA answers or performs the task
App checks required steps against correct_response and office rules
App shows missing or incorrect steps
VA repeats immediately with a new scenario (repeat variant)
VA writes the workflow SOP after the workflow's last scheduled scenario
Doctor approves, corrects or rejects the SOP
App marks the workflow Certified, Retrain or Pending
certification.repeat_rule: Any situational answer scored below 2 triggers an immediate repeat with a new scenario for the same item (same correct_response, new patient/time/details, generated per office and approved by VFDA). Both scores are stored and reported, e.g. 'A6: 1/2 first try, 2/2 on repeat'.
certification.day_score_rule: The day's pass/fail uses first-try scores. A day still passes only if every missed item was corrected on repeat (repeat score 2/2) and there were no critical errors.
certification.workflow_certified_when: All of the workflow's scenarios across the schedule are first-try passed or corrected on repeat, zero critical errors, workflow pass_standard met, and the doctor approved the VA's SOP.
certification.retrain_when: A critical error, a repeat still below 2/2, or the doctor rejects the SOP.
certification.pending_when: Scenarios done but SOP not yet approved, or the workflow's later days not yet reached.
report_fields: items repeated with first and repeat scores
critical errors with the VA's exact words
certification.navigation_rule: VAs are not graded on exact buttons. When a scenario involves the EHR, texting or phone system, the VA describes how they'd do it in their own words; grading checks the approach, order, verification and documentation, not click paths.

grading.situational_rubric: 2 = right approach and every required step (in order, with verification and documentation) per the office's rules; 1 = partial or a step missed/out of order; 0 = wrong action
rules: Check the critical fail first; if triggered the quiz fails and the report quotes the VA's exact words
Grade against the office's interview answers, not general best practice
Name the missed point in one line for any item under 2
Don't penalize wording, grammar or English level
grading.result: pass if points >= pass_points and no critical error; review if points >= review_min_points or any low-confidence item; else retake (version B next day)

doctor_flow.rule: The doctor never sees the full list of rule slots.
steps: Office setup: 8 profile questions
VFDA uploads card PDFs; Claude extracts doctor-tier rules and VFDA reviews them
Doctor confirms extracted rules one screen per card group (Looks right / Edit), with only not-found or conflicting rules shown as questions
Doctor sees one 'VFDA standards' page listing default-tier rules, pre-accepted; 'Accept all' or edit any
Auto-tier rules are filled by VFDA or derived and never shown
doctor_flow.default_tier_behaviour: Default-tier rules are accepted automatically with source vfda_default. Card import may override a default if the doctor's cards state something different; that override is shown on the VFDA standards page.
